subject.title: feat: context provenance metadata for injected bootstrap segments

question: Should OpenClaw adopt model-visible `ctx:provenance` HTML comments for bootstrap context as the Phase 1 contract, or pause this branch in favor of a runtime-owned freshness design?
rationale: The patch is a coherent feature candidate, but it changes the model-visible context/session contract and now intersects with current prompt-cache boundary behavior that did not exist in the same shape when the branch was opened.

options.title: Pause for provenance direction
options.body: Keep the RFC and PR open while a maintainer chooses inline tags versus runtime-owned freshness before more implementation churn.

options.title: Adopt inline Phase 1 after rebase
options.body: Ask for a rebase onto current main plus real prompt-output proof, then review the updated implementation against stable and dynamic context placement.

options.title: Close in favor of a different design
options.body: If maintainers reject model-visible tags, close this PR and keep the RFC or a new issue for the chosen runtime-owned approach.

recommendation.title: Pause for provenance direction
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC and PR open while a maintainer chooses inline tags versus runtime-owned freshness before more implementation churn.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent refactor history put the affected prompt/bootstrap context surfaces under recent work by steipete.
